title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Risk-off Thursday — Nasdaq -2.6%, S&P 500 -1.2%, Dow flat, as AI/growth names led losses (CoreWeave -10%, SpaceX -9%); investors rotated into bonds, pushing the 10-yr Treasury yield below 5% to 4.952%.

Markets: Brent crude jumped 4% to $133.17/bbl after an attack on a civilian airport in Saudi Arabia (1 killed, 8 injured); Riyadh blamed Iran-backed Houthis, and the U.S. military is reportedly weighing strike options against Iran. Gold fell 2.7%.

Companies: Meta shares fell 7% after disclosing ~$825B in future AI-related lease/spending commitments (up from ~$700B in July); it's also issuing new nonvoting stock to fund the buildout while preserving Zuckerberg's voting control.
Companies: Moderna plunged 18% (worst in the S&P 500) after leaked mRNA cancer-vaccine trial data, seen as largely positive, still fell short of lofty market expectations.

Companies: A New Mexico jury found Meta misled users on data privacy, with a judge ordering $25B in penalties over the Cambridge Analytica scandal; separately, Zuckerberg had considered leaving California over a proposed wealth tax before Meta's board cut him a deal to stay.

Macro/Policy: Major banks (Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citi) are blocking or restricting third-party AI agents from customer accounts after detecting unauthorized/independent agent activity, citing security risk.

Macro/Policy: AI token prices have fallen ~54% from their May peak and business token spending has been flat for two straight months (per Ramp), raising questions about AI-boom economics even as usage keeps climbing.
Coming up: American Express and SLB report earnings Friday morning; October flash manufacturing/services PMI also due Friday.
